blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Estimating 3D head expression from a single image requires mapping visual appearance to underlying facial geometry. We propose ViGA-FLAME, a two-stage framework that aligns semantic visual features with a structured geometric latent space. First, a Parametric-Geometric Variational Autoencoder (PG-VAE) learns a unified representation of canonical head surfaces and FLAME parameters, supporting both detailed surface reconstruction and interpretable parameter recovery. Supervision on geometry and parameters, together with consistency between the two decoding branches, connects surface detail with parametric structure. Second, a trainable Visual-Geometric Adapter (ViGA) maps features from a pretrained semantic visual encoder into this latent space. Asymmetric attention enables ViGA to align semantic image features from the visual encoder with the structured geometric information represented in the PG-VAE latent space, without altering the original visual stream. By grounding image evidence in this latent prior, ViGA-FLAME enables robust 3D head expression estimation across severe facial deformations and large viewing angles, efficiently improving robustness over competing feed-forward methods.
blocks.zh: 从一幅图像中估计出3D头部表情需要将视觉外观映射到基本的面部几何. 我们提议ViGA-FLAME,一种将语义视觉特征与结构化几何潜在空间相协调的两相框架. 首先,一个参数-几何变量自动编码器(PG-VAE)学习了对犬头表面和FLAME参数的统一表示,支持详细的地表重建以及可解释参数恢复. 对几何和参数的监督,加上两个解码分支的一致性,将表面细节与参数结构相接. 其次,一个可被训练的可视-几何适配器(ViGA)将预先训练的语义视觉编码器的特征映射入了这个潜在的空间. 不对称的注意使得ViGA能够将视觉编码器中的语义图像特征与PG-VAE潜在空间中所代表的结构几何信息相配合,而不会改变原始的视觉流. ViGA-FLAME通过将图像证据置入这一潜在的前作,使得在严重面部变形和大取景角度上能够进行强力的3D头部表达估计,比起相竞争的向馈方法,有效地提高强力.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Recovering 3D head geometry and expression from a single image is challenging because facial appearance entangles identity, expression, pose, and viewpoint, while self-occlusion conceals surface deformations. FLAME [ 6 ] provides a compact, animatable representation of these factors, yet reliably inferring its parameters remains difficult under extreme expressions and profile views.
Predicting FLAME parameters from images requires visual features that capture appearance cues and a geometric prior for 3D interpretation.
blocks.zh:
从单一图像中恢复3D头几何和表达方式具有挑战性,因为面部外观缠绕了身份,表情,姿势和观点,而自闭则会隐藏出表面变形. FLAME [6]提供了对这些因素的紧凑、可想象的表述,但可靠地推断其参数在极端表达和剖面观点下仍然很困难。
从图像中预测FLAME参数需要捕捉出外观提示的视觉特征,以及3D解释前的几何.

blocks.en:
Existing FLAME estimation methods rely on either optimization or feed-forward prediction.
Optimization-based approaches minimize landmark [ 2 , 8 ] , photometric [ 15 ] , and appearance objectives [ 10 ] for each input image.
Although flexible, these methods incur substantial test-time cost and can be sensitive to initialization, occlusion, and rendering mismatch. Feed-forward methods directly regress parameters or geometry: DECA [ 3 ] predicts FLAME parameters and geometric-detail codes, SMIRK [ 11 ] and TEASER [ 7 ] leverage appearance-aware supervision for expression recovery, and
SHeaP [ 13 ] learns a 3D morphable-model predictor through reanimation-based self-supervision with 3DMM-rigged 2D Gaussian rendering.
However, these methods typically regress FLAME parameters directly from image features, without first organizing dense geometry and parametric factors in a shared latent representation.
blocks.zh:
现有的FLAME估计方法依赖优化或向导预测.
基于优化的方法将标志性[2,8],光度[15],以及每个输入图像的外观目标[10]最小化.
这些方法虽然灵活,但需要花费大量的试验时间,对初始化、隔离和造成不匹配十分敏感。 Feed-forward方法直接倒置参数或几何:DECA [3] 预测FLAME参数和几何-细节代码,SMIRK [11]和TEASER [7] 杠杆外观-知觉监督用于表达恢复,以及
SHeaP [13] 通过以再生为主的自超能,用3DMM-riged 2D Gaussian渲染来学习出一个3D可变模型预测器.
然而,这些方法通常直接从图像特征中倒退出FLAME参数,而没有首先在共同的潜在代表中组织密集的几何和参数因素.

blocks.en:
We propose ViGA-FLAME, a feed-forward framework that maps images into a learned parametric-geometric latent space for 3D head reconstruction.
First, PG-VAE learns a unified parametric-geometric latent space from canonical FLAME surfaces, jointly supporting dense geometric reconstruction with parametric decoding. Second, ViGA augments a frozen image encoder (Sapiens2 [ 4 ] ) with a read-only side-branch adapter, whose semantic and geometric tokens extract visual features without modifying the backbone and project them into the PG-VAE latent space. By aligning visual features with this geometric prior, ViGA-FLAME transfers image context to structured prediction, enabling surface reconstruction and FLAME parameter recovery in a single forward pass.
Our contributions are threefold:
(1) PG-VAE, which unifies dense geometry and parametric FLAME representations;
(2) ViGA, a read-only adapter that aligns visual features with the geometric latent space; and
(3) extensive experiments demonstrating improved accuracy and robustness across shape, expression, pose, and viewpoint variations.
blocks.zh:
我们提出ViGA-FLAME,这是一个向导框架,将图像映射到一个三维头部重建的已学到的参数几何潜入空间。
首先,PG-VAE从舟体FLAME表面学习出统一的参数-几何潜入空间,用参数解码共同支持密度几何重建. 第二,VIGA用只读的侧分机适配器来增强被冻结的图像编码器(Sapiens2 [4]),其语义和几何符号在不修改主干线的情况下取出可视特性并投放入PG-VAE潜入空间. 通过将视觉特征与这个几何前置,ViGA-FLAME将图像上下文传输到结构化的预测上,使得表面重建以及FLAME参数在单一前行中恢复.
我们的贡献有三:
(1) PG-VAE,它统一了密度几何和参数FLAME的表示;
(2) ViGA,一种只读适配器,使视觉特征与几何潜入空间相配合;以及
(3) 进行广泛的实验,表明在形状、表情、姿势和观点变化方面精确度和稳健性得到提高。

blocks.en: 2 Proposed Method
blocks.zh: 2 拟议方法

blocks.en: As shown in Fig. 1 , our framework first learns a unified parametric-geometric prior from canonical FLAME surfaces using PG-VAE. ViGA then predicts the corresponding latent representation from a single image by aligning visual features with the learned latent space, enabling decoding into either FLAME parameters or dense surface vertices.
blocks.zh: 如图1所示,我们的框架首先从犬科FLAME表面使用PG-VAE来学习一个统一的参数几何. VIGA随后通过将视觉特征与所学到的潜入空间相配合来预测单个图像的相应潜在代表,从而可以解码为FLAME参数或密集的表面顶点.

blocks.en: Figure 1: Method overview . We first introduce PG-VAE (Sec. 2.1 ) to learn a unified geometric representation from canonical FLAME surfaces. We then align its frozen representation with image features using the ViGA-FLAME, described in Sec. 2.2 .
blocks.zh: 图1:方法概述 我们首先引入了PG-VAE(sec. 2.1),从犬科FLAME表面学习出统一的几何表示. 然后,我们利用第2.2.节所述的VIGA-FLAME,使其被冻结的表示与图像特性一致。

blocks.en: 2.1 PG-VAE: Unified Geometry and FLAME Representation
blocks.zh: 2.1 PG-VAE:统一几何和FLAME代表

blocks.en: Parametric head models [ 6 ] provide interpretable control but constrain geometric expressivity, whereas non-parametric surfaces preserve detail without semantic factorization. PG-VAE aims to combine both by learning a unified latent representation with geometric tokens for dense surface reconstruction and semantic tokens for FLAME parameter recovery.
blocks.zh: 参数头模型 [6] 提供了可解释控制但制约了几何表达性,而非参数面则保存了细节而无语义因子化. PG-VAE旨在结合两种方法,一是学习一种统一的潜能表示,一是密集地进行地表重建的几何符号;一是FLAME参数恢复的语义符号.

blocks.en:
Model Architecture. PG-VAE learns a joint parametric-geometric tokenized representation from a canonical, root-centered FLAME mesh ℳ = ( V , E ) \mathcal{M}=(V,E) , where V ∈ ℝ N × 3 V\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 3} contains N = 5023 N=5023 vertex coordinates and E E denotes the fixed FLAME face connectivity. Fourier features and linear projections encode the vertex coordinates V V into point features P ∈ ℝ N × d e P\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d_{e}} , where d e d_{e} is the encoder channel size.
The encoder comprises four parameter-conditioned semantic queries and N g N_{g} learnable geometric queries. Specifically, the FLAME parameters are denoted by { β , r , ψ , J } \{\beta,r,\psi,J\} , where β \beta and ψ \psi represent shape and expression coefficients, r r contains the global orientation together with the rotations of the key FLAME joints, and J J denotes the corresponding joint positions. Four independent MLPs project these factors into shape, rotation, expression, and position queries, respectively: Q e ​ n ​ c = [ q shap , q rot , q exp , q pos , q 1 geo , … , q N g geo ] ⊤ . (1) The queries aggregate point features through cross-attention and interact through self-attention, yielding a variational token latent Z Z .
PG-VAE uses geometric and parametric decoders.
The geometric decoder D geo D_{\mathrm{geo}} performs explicit fixed-topology mesh decoding.
It uses N N learnable vertex-indexed queries Q dec = [ q 1 dec , … , q N dec ] ⊤ Q^{\mathrm{dec}}=[q^{\mathrm{dec}}_{1},\ldots,q^{\mathrm{dec}}_{N}]^{\top} , with one query associated with each fixed FLAME vertex index. These queries cross-attend to the decoded latent tokens and regress the corresponding canonical vertex coordinates, yielding V ^ geo = D geo ​ ( Z , Q dec ) ∈ ℝ N × 3 \hat{V}_{\mathrm{geo}}=D_{\mathrm{geo}}(Z,Q^{\mathrm{dec}})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 3} .
This explicit ordered-vertex decoding preserves fixed FLAME vertex correspondence while coupling dense geometric reconstruction with interpretable parametric factors.

blocks.en:
First, the geometric branch is supervised by a vertex-wise Huber loss ℒ geo \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{geo}} between V ^ geo \hat{V}_{\mathrm{geo}} and V gt V_{\mathrm{gt}} . Since all meshes share the FLAME topology, this loss directly compares corresponding vertex coordinates and encourages the geometric tokens to preserve fine-grained surface deformations.
Second, ℒ flame \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{flame}} supervises the FLAME predictions: mean-squared error for shape/expression coefficients, S ​ O ​ ( 3 ) SO(3) geodesic distance for global orientation and joint rotations, and Huber loss for joint positions. This term encourages the semantic tokens to retain explicit control over identity, expression, and articulation.
Third, parameter-space supervision alone is insufficient because equal errors in different FLAME coefficients can induce substantially different surface deformations. We therefore decode the predicted parameters into V ^ par \hat{V}_{\mathrm{par}} and impose a vertex-wise Huber loss ℒ par ​ - ​ gt \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{par\text{-}gt}} against V gt V_{\mathrm{gt}} . This decoded-surface loss grounds parametric estimation in canonical 3D geometry rather than solely in coefficient space.
Fourth, to couple the two branches, we apply a consistency loss ℒ par ​ - ​ geo \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{par\text{-}geo}} between V ^ par \hat{V}_{\mathrm{par}} and V ^ geo \hat{V}_{\mathrm{geo}} .
Finally, the KL divergence ℒ KL \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{KL}} regularizes the variational posterior toward a unit Gaussian prior.
To summarize, the overall objective of PG-VAE is: ℒ PG = ℒ geo + λ f ​ ℒ flame + λ g ​ ℒ par ​ - ​ gt + λ c ​ ℒ par ​ - ​ geo + β ​ ℒ KL , \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{PG}}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{geo}}+\lambda_{f}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{flame}}+\lambda_{g}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{par\text{-}gt}}+\lambda_{c}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{par\text{-}geo}}+\beta\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{KL}}, (2) where λ f \lambda_{f} , λ g \lambda_{g} , λ c \lambda_{c} and β \beta are hyperparameters. blocks.en: 2.2 ViGA: Visual-to-Geometric Adapter
blocks.zh: 2.2 ViGA:可视对测适应器

blocks.en: We design a Visual-to-Geometric Adapter (ViGA) to predict the corresponding PG-VAE latent vectors from a single image. ViGA is attached to a pretrained visual Transformer, using Sapiens2 [ 4 ] as the backbone. With the backbone fully frozen, ViGA reads intermediate token features through a side branch without modifying the original parameters, token states, or outputs. This asymmetric design preserves the pretrained semantic representation while enabling ViGA tokens to aggregate contextual visual cues for latent alignment.
blocks.zh: 我们设计了一个可视到几何适应器(ViGA),从一幅图像中预测相应的PG-VAE潜在向量. ViGA被附着在被预先训练的视觉变形器上,以Sapians2 [4]为骨干. 在主干被完全冻结后,VIGA通过一个侧分支读取中间符号特性,而不修改原始参数,符号状态,或输出. 这种不对称设计保留了被事先训练的语义表现,同时使VIGA符号能够将上下文的视觉提示集为潜在对齐.

blocks.en:

Let X l X^{l} denote the native token sequence of the frozen visual encoder at layer l l . ViGA introduces an extra token sequence Y l = [ F l ; G l ] Y^{l}=[F^{l};G^{l}] ,
where F l F^{l} denotes the hidden features of the four FLAME-semantic tokens and G l G^{l} denotes those of the geometric tokens.
At each visual-encoder layer, the frozen backbone follows its original forward pass, while ViGA updates only its geometric stream:

blocks.en: 2.3 Training Data Synthesis
blocks.zh: 2.3 培训数据综合

blocks.en: We generate training pairs by sampling FLAME parameters and rendering corresponding images with Nvdiffrast [ 5 ] , which provides exact correspondence among images, canonical surfaces, and FLAME parameters. We randomize identity, expression, local pose, texture [ 1 ] , hair [ 12 ] , background, and illumination to improve appearance diversity. PG-VAE is trained on FLAME surfaces sampled online, whereas ViGA is trained on 100 100 K rendered images at 768 × 1024 768\times 1024 resolution.
blocks.zh: 我们通过取样FLAME参数和用Nvdiffrast[5]绘制相应的图像生成训练对子,这些图像提供了图像、犬形表面和FLAME参数之间的精确对应。 我们随机划分身份,表达,局部姿势,纹理[1],发[12],背景,并进行照明来提高外观多样性. PG-VAE接受在线取样的FLAME表面培训,而ViGA则接受100克制成图像的培训,分辨率为768×1024 768\times 1024。

blocks.en: 3 Experiments
blocks.zh: 3个实验

blocks.en: 3.1 Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 3.1 执行细节

blocks.en:
We initialize PG-VAE attention layers from Hunyuan3D 2.0 [ 14 ] and optimize newly introduced and transferred parameters using AdamW with learning rates of 10 − 4 10^{-4} and 10 − 5 10^{-5} , respectively, 500 500 warm-up steps, a weight decay of 0.01 0.01 , and a global batch size of 1024 1024 .
ViGA is trained on 768 × 1024 768\times 1024 images using AdamW with a learning rate of 10 − 4 10^{-4} , weight decay 0.05 0.05 , and a global batch size of 256 256 . Both stages use bfloat16 mixed-precision training on 4 NVIDIA H200 GPUs.

ViGA在768×1024 768\times 1024图像上接受训练,使用AdamW,学习率为10−4 10^{-4},重量衰减0.050.05,全球分批大小为256 256. 两个阶段都使用bfloat16混合精度训练来进行4个NVIDIA H200 GPU.

blocks.en: 3.2 Single-Image FLAME Parameter Estimation
blocks.zh: 3.2 单一形象FLAME 参数估计

blocks.en:
We evaluate whether the learned representation generalizes beyond the FLAME2023 geometry used to train our model. We construct a controlled synthetic benchmark with random FLAME parameters. For each identity, we render five fixed camera views corresponding to frontal ( 0 ∘ 0^{\circ} ), oblique ( ± 45 ∘ \pm 45^{\circ} ), and profile ( ± 90 ∘ \pm 90^{\circ} ) observations.
We synthesise head variations by sampling FLAME shape, expression, and pose parameters under five regimes: all typical , shape extreme , expression extreme , pose extreme , and all extreme . Each regime contains 50 50 instances. All factors remain within their typical ranges in all typical , while only the specified factor is extreme in each single-factor regime and all factors are extreme in all extreme . For shape and expression,
typical PCA coefficients lie within 2.5 ​ σ 2.5\sigma ; extreme shape/expression regimes set at least one leading 20 20 coefficient between 2.5 ​ σ 2.5\sigma and 3.5 ​ σ 3.5\sigma , while extreme pose regimes use rotations near the physical limits of the neck, jaw, and eyes. Real-world evaluations use RenderMe360 [ 9 ] .
We compare the reconstruction and parametric outputs of ViGA-FLAME with FLAME-based regressors: DECA [ 3 ] , SMIRK [ 11 ] , TEASER [ 7 ] , and SHeaP [ 13 ] . We evaluate only a common face-only surface region. Each predicted surface is aligned to the FLAME ground-truth face mesh using rigid ICP with rotation and translation only. We report the averaged symmetric Chamfer-L1 distance (CD-L1, mm) and the F-score at a 5 5 mm threshold (F@5).

blocks.en:
As shown in Table 1 , both ViGA-FLAME outputs outperform all baselines across the synthetic regimes, with the parametric branch achieving the strongest results under the most challenging all extreme setting, highlighting robustness when shape, expression, and pose vary jointly.
Table 2 further shows that the parametric branch achieves the best reconstruction accuracy at frontal, oblique, and profile viewpoints.
On the real-world RenderMe360 dataset, our parametric branch surpasses SMIRK and TEASER, though trailing DECA and SHeaP. This transfer is notable as ViGA-FLAME is trained exclusively on synthetic renders, whereas baselines leverage real-image supervision or self-supervision. The residual gap reflects limited synthetic appearance diversity (e.g., heavy makeup, age-related skin textures), pointing to data augmentation rather than a flaw in our latent-alignment formulation.
Moreover, optimization-based methods rely on 2D landmark fitting, whose localization becomes unreliable under oblique and profile views due to severe self-occlusion. We therefore restrict quantitative comparisons to feed-forward methods operating under a matched single-image inference protocol.
blocks.zh:
如表1所示,VIGA-FLAME的输出都超过了合成系统的所有基线,在最具有挑战性的所有极端环境下,参数分支都取得了最强的成果,突出在形状、表情和姿势变化时的稳健性。
表2还显示,参数分支在前方、斜面和剖面角度上达到最好的重建精度。
在现实世界的RenderMe360数据集上,我们的参数分支超越了SMIRK和TEASER,虽然跟随DECA和SHeaP. 这种转移是值得注意的,因为VIGA-FLAME只接受合成材料的培训,而基线则利用真实图像监督或自我监督。 剩余差距反映了有限的合成外观多样性(例如:重妆、与年龄有关的皮肤纹理),表明数据增强,而不是我们潜在对齐配方的缺陷。
此外,以优化为基础的方法依赖于2D地标相配,由于严重的自闭症,其本地化在直观和剖面观点下变得不可靠. 因此,我们将定量比较限制在根据匹配的单一图像推论协议运作的向馈法。

blocks.en:
We compare unconditional learnable semantic embeddings with parameter-conditioned semantic tokens. Replacing semantic query embeddings with factor-specific MLP projections of FLAME factors achieves the best performance on all metrics, outperforming additive fusion.
Thus, factor-specific conditioning provides a stronger inductive bias for organizing semantic token slots and aligning parametric decoding with dense geometric reconstruction.

因此,因子特定条件为组织语义符号槽和使参数解码与密集几何重建相协调提供了更强的诱导偏差.

blocks.en: 4 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 4 结论

blocks.en: We present ViGA-FLAME, a feed-forward framework aligning a frozen image encoder with PG-VAE’s joint parametric-geometric latent space, enabling dense surface reconstruction and FLAME estimation from a single image. Experiments demonstrate improved robustness under controlled variations in shape, expression, pose, and viewpoint, while showing transfer to real-world head estimation.
blocks.zh: 我们提出ViGA-FLAME,这是一个向导的框架,它使一个被冻结的图像编码器与PG-VAE的联合参数-几何潜入空间相配合,从而能够从单一的图像中进行密集的地表重建和FLAME估计。 实验显示,在形状、表情、姿势和观点的可控变化下,稳健性有所提高,同时显示向现实世界头部估计的转移。
